proposed_candidates.prompt_content: When an execution unit authors or modifies a precommitted schedule, history commitment, salt, or any ordering that later selects targets or truncates search, derive that value only from stable behavior semantics: program descriptors, support examples, domains, and digest-ranked schedule content. Never fold whole run reports, engine run ids, trial-ledger bytes, timestamps, or other per-process values into such a commitment; a reproducibility check (two fresh processes, identical seed and tree, identical selection) is part of the unit's evidence. The compliant in-repo pattern is evidence_derived_target_synthesis.py; the violation pattern to avoid is folding a full evidence report digest into a selection salt.
proposed_candidates.risk: An over-broad reading could forbid legitimate audit digests or force sorting costs onto hot paths; the rule therefore binds only values consumed by selection, ordering, or truncation, and the reproducibility check bounds the trial cost to one duplicate process run per authored commitment.
proposed_candidates.rollback_conditions: Reject for scope if a trial shows the rule blocks a commitment that is genuinely per-run by design (none known), or if the reproducibility check proves too expensive relative to unit runtime on two consecutive trials.
supporting_evidence: Live divergence: two identical-seed, identical-tree runs of run_recursive_evidence_frontier_growth selected different recursive targets (sub- vs mul-wrap), recorded in this episode and in merged PR 245's corrected body
